clue.text: Place containing tiny back room

indicators.note: the place word holds the next piece inside it, as a box contains its contents

parts.note: to lay something is to place it

indicators.note: going back means the small word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for very small

explanation.surface: An estate agent's listing: a home whose box room is tiny and tucked at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back room' reads as one phrase, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay and 'room' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is slack or margin for manoeuvre, which is the figurative sense of room.

clue.text: Flies flying round the French flat

indicators.note: things flying about are scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order
the rearranged letters go round, enclosing, the next piece

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: Flies buzzing around a French apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' looks like an article plus adjective, but together they mean the French for 'the', and 'flat' is not an apartment but the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull performance or a drink gone stale can be called flat, meaning without vitality, synonymous with lifeless.

clue.text: Mistake admitted by conjuror, really upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run from bottom to top
what is admitted by the words is let in among them, sitting inside the following letters

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second run together

explanation.surface: A magician who fumbles a trick is genuinely distressed by the blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Shocking times, wearing a shortened mini!

indicators.note: the first piece is wearing the rest, so it sits inside them as a body inside clothes
shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
mini means small
times as in multiplication: three by four

explanation.surface: A disapproving exclamation about hemlines in an era of very short miniskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini' looks like the skirt; it is just the adjective for little, cut to four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly bad, and shocking in British speech is an informal word for very bad.

clue.text: Lead in Otello, part he developed carrying a gibus

indicators.note: the developed letters carry the next piece within them
something developed is worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
the lead of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Verdi's opera title
taken as written
taken as written, the first of the two a's in the clue

explanation.surface: The tenor singing Otello works up his role while holding a collapsible top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two a's: the one after 'carrying' joins the anagram letters, and the one before 'gibus' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibus is a collapsible top hat worn to evening performances, named after its French inventor, hence the name opera hat.

clue.text: Operate without assistance, as one into patience will

parts.note: the plain meaning: do something entirely by yourself
patience is the British name for solitaire, a card game one deals and plays alone

explanation.walkthrough: 'patience' suggests the virtue, but it is the one-player card game, so a fan of it literally plays cards with nobody else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from card games where one player plays a hand without a partner, meaning to act independently.

clue.text: Nastier fizzy Greek wine

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a sparkling Greek wine tastes even worse than the still kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, a specific example of the wine named.

clue.text: Recently stolen on Jersey? That could be a controversial issue

parts.note: stolen goods still being traced are called hot
the Jersey Royal is a famous new potato grown on the Channel island

explanation.surface: A theft on the island of Jersey becomes a sensitive local matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests a sweater or the island; here it stands for its famous potato, the Jersey Royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a delicate topic that everyone wants to avoid handling.

clue.text: Aim at goal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to direct effort or fire towards
second meaning: an objective one is trying to reach

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a football instruction to shoot; the phrasal verb and the noun are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a verb for aiming at something and as a noun for the objective itself.

clue.text: Plant, rosy in bloom, Faith cultivated outside

indicators.note: a flower in bloom has opened out of its bud shape, so these letters take a new form
cultivated ground is turned over, so these letters are turned into a new order
the second rearranged group goes outside, wrapping around the first

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener named Faith grows a pink flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub with bright yellow spring flowers, so it is one example of a plant.

clue.text: Not at all credible, bird under car being clipped

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end trimmed off, so the last letter goes
in a down answer, something under another sits below it, so the bird piece comes second

parts.note: a hardtop is a car with a rigid fixed roof
the swallow is a migratory bird

explanation.surface: An implausible tale of a bird struck by a passing car.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' puts the bird below the car piece; the bird-and-car story itself is the hard-to-believe tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to swallow is an idiom for a claim that is difficult to accept or believe.

clue.text: Master has little time during bad defeat to be upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the defeat word is turned round
something happening during another thing occurs within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has a brief spell of distress after a heavy sporting loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a teacher, and master is the older British word for a male schoolteacher.

clue.text: One who makes a bit?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who earns a little money, or does a small amount
the setter's reading: a bit is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle, and this craftsman makes them

explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a bit' sounds like earning a little cash; the bit is horse tack, and the answer is an old trade name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorimer is a maker of bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horse harness, an old craft guild title.

clue.text: Notice one model is fatty

parts.note: a notice in a paper is an advertisement, an ad
the Roman numeral for one
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: A gossip remark that a particular fashion model has put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes tissue made of or storing fat, the technical adjective for fatty.

clue.text: A Vivien Leigh role, as Charlotte, baroque artist

indicators.note: baroque means extravagantly ornate and twisted, so these letters are worked into an elaborate new order

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, the standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: An actress playing a part named Charlotte in a baroque-era drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque artist' reads as one painter; 'baroque' shuffles the two preceding words and 'artist' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivien Leigh won an Oscar playing the heroine of Gone with the Wind, her most famous film role.

clue.text: Unexpectedly relaxed about article, the leader of the band?

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome comes out differently, so these letters arrive in another order
the rearranged letters sit about, surrounding, the article

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A laid-back bandleader who turns out surprisingly easygoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Irving Berlin's song is Alexander's Ragtime Band, so its leader owns the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title Alexander's Ragtime Band implies a bandleader of that first name, so the playful definition points to it.

clue.text: Sailors aboard vessel, science fiction craft

indicators.note: people aboard a vessel are inside it, so the crew word goes within

parts.note: a ship is a seagoing vessel
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Crew members on board a spaceship from a sci-fi story.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a fictional spacecraft able to travel between stars, a staple of space opera.

clue.text: Magazine's article about me in a Cheshire town

indicators.note: the magazine piece goes about, surrounding, the word me

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine, plus the possessive s
taken as written
a newspaper or magazine article is a report

explanation.surface: A magazine runs a feature about the writer set in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine's article is one combined piece that wraps around the self-reference. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellesmere Port is an industrial town on the Manchester Ship Canal in the county of Cheshire.

clue.text: US writer's come over to be entertained by fat cat

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is received inside the host's home

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: something that has come over has flipped, so the writer's name runs backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, American author

explanation.surface: An American author visits to be wined and dined by a rich, powerful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' reads as a wealthy fat cat; 'fat' is the wordplay and 'cat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a big spotted wild cat of Africa and Asia, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Man sees shapes in a body

indicators.note: to shape something is to mould it anew, so these letters are formed into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone glimpses figures moving within a body, like a ghost story or an X-ray.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English meaning all together as a group, as one body.

clue.text: Discrimination shown in shocking images

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, so the letters are knocked into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Offensive pictures reveal prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people because of their age, one form of discrimination.

clue.text: Breakfast dish made by great Italian round Los Angeles

parts.note: gran is Italian for great, as in Gran Turismo
the letter O is round in shape
the standard abbreviation for the city

explanation.surface: A celebrated Italian chef cooks breakfast around Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great Italian' suggests a famous person from Italy; it means the Italian word for great.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is baked oats, nuts and honey, eaten as a cereal in the morning, so it is one breakfast food.

clue.text: Former social worker without equal, covering miles on runs

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so the first word wraps the next piece

parts.note: alone in one's class, peerless
M is the abbreviation for miles
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An unrivalled former caseworker who covers great distances on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Almoners were British hospital officials handling patients' welfare, a role now done by medical social workers.

clue.text: Diana disguised as a nymph

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters are rearranged to look different

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana in costume as one of the lesser woodland spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, presiding over a spring or river.

clue.text: Country home needs help sent over

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: sent over means flipped across, so the help word is read from the end

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A rural household requires assistance to be dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation of South Asia, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Dame's with German husband in siege town

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady, plus the possessive s
mit is the German for with
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A titled woman and her German spouse are trapped in a besieged town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' seems a joining word; with 'German' it means the German word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladysmith in South Africa was besieged by Boer forces for four months in 1899-1900.

clue.text: Discount boy not working

parts.note: Mark is a boy's name
a system that is down is out of action

explanation.surface: A cut-price deal on a lad who is unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: A markdown is a reduction in a price, the same idea as a discount.

clue.text: Make fun of post at college

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Mocking someone by mail while studying at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is a British idiom for parodying or satirising someone, which mocks them.
